summary: Shunji Hosaka specializes in religious studies, Indology, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Waseda University (~1975–1980), he held posts at Reitaku University (~1990–2004) and Chuo University (~2004–2021).

Shunkyo Katsumata was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1931–1934). He held posts at Toyo University and Taisho University (~1948–1985), where he served as professor emeritus.
Shunpaku Nakao is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as an assistant professor (attested 1963) and professor (attested 1976) at Shuchiin University.

Shunryu Suzuki worked in Buddhist studies, studying at Komazawa University and Eihei-ji, and under teachers including Gyokujun So-on and Ian Kishizawa. He served as abbot at Zoun-in, Rinsō-in, and Sōkō-ji, and founded the San Francisco Zen Center.

Shunsho Manabe worked in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He studied at Tohoku University (~1961–1968) and held posts at Hosen Gakuen College (~1978–2004) and Shikoku University (~2004–2017) as professor.
Shunsho Terakawa was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1951–1956) and held a post at Otani University (~1960–2000), where he became emeritus professor.
Shuntaro Kondo is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Ryukoku University by 2011 and served there as a part-time lecturer (attested 2012).

Shuntaro Matsuyama worked in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Naoshiro Tsuji and held posts at Bigakko, Kokugakuin University, Tama Art University, and Joshibi University of Art and Design (~1980–1996).

Shunzo Onoda is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his D.Lit. from Bukkyo University by 1993 and served there as associate professor (attested 1996) and professor (attested 2005).

Shuyu Kanaoka was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1948–1952) and Toyo University (doctorate, 1962). He served as an assistant professor at Toyo University (~1965–1992).
Shuyu Sakurai, a Buddhist studies scholar, studied at Tohoku University (~1940–1943) and served as emeritus professor at Komazawa University (~1950–1987).
Shwe Zan Aung worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned a B.A. from the University of Rangoon (~1888–1891) and studied under traditional teachers U Gandama and Ledi Sayadaw in 1895.
Shōkō Kabutogi was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University (~1932–1936) and later served there as a professor (~1950–1982).

Shōren Ihara was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Kyushu University, including assistant professor (attested 1959–1965), and was a member at the Naritasan Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 1996–1998).

Shōyū Hanayama was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1950–1959). He served as vice president at Musashino University (~1968–1995) and chairperson at Bukkyo Dendo Kyokai (~1993–1995).

Si Ti La is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a PhD at Acharya Nagarjuna University under J. Sitaramamma (attested 2014) and studied under multiple traditional teachers, including Sayadaw U Kundala and Sayadaw U Ghosita.

Sibani Das Gupta specialized in Indology, studying at the University of Dhaka and under Rajendra Chandra Hazra. She completed a doctorate at the University of Calcutta by 1954 under the supervision of Sushil Kumar De.

Sibaraj Chetry is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who studied under Sibnath Sarma, D. K. Chakravarty, and others. He served as a lecturer of philosophy at North Lakhimpur College (attested 2012).

Sibnath Sarma is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He held posts at the Research and Archaeological Department, Jammu and Kashmir, and served as a professor in the Department of Philosophy at Gauhati University (attested 1999–2012).
Sibylle Koch is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied at the University of Oxford and completed an MA at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (2012–2015).
